mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to higher discount rates eroding future earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting stronger labor market confidence and corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 over the next month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following the trigger, forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) even when PAYEMS meets the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1,350 in a month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive, indicating resilient consumer demand supporting corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: Over multiple 60-day periods with the trigger, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (mean return ≤ baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% over two months suggests supply-side weakness, leading to a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% over the next two months
failure_condition: During such supply shocks, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 3.0% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is predicted to be positive due to reduced labor market friction and stronger investor sentiment.
failure_condition: In the 5-day windows following the trigger, forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% and 5%, respectively, over the next quarter suggest dual demand drivers and a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥2% AND RSAFS increases by ≥5% over the next 3 months
failure_condition: During the 20-day horizon after the interaction trigger, forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp spike in CPIAUCSL (CPI) above 260 points for two consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 60-day forward return due to expectations of higher inflation and tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: In 60-day windows with the trigger, forward returns are not significantly negative (mean return ≥ baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of INDPRO to GDPC1 falls below 0.85 for 10 consecutive trading days, it indicates supply chain compression and a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: During the 20-day window with the interaction trigger, forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
